newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour welcomes approach from small Alliance.
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour welcomes approach from small Alliance.

text.p: New Zealand's main opposition Labour Party welcomed a weekend change of stance by the leader of the smaller, broad-left Alliance grouping that indicated it was ready to team up with Labour after the next election.
The Alliance's Jim Anderton told a conference on Saturday he was changing tactics to help the grouping become "part of the positive alternative" to the current centre-right government.

In the run-up to last year's general election -- the first under the country's version of proportional representation -- the Alliance insisted on seeking a pre-ballot policy deal, while Labour said it would only negotiate after the result.
In the event, the main centre-right National Party formed a coalition with the small nationalist party New Zealand First after a frenzied spell of multi-party negotiations.
Labour has since caught up with National in opinion polls, and overtook it by a wide margin in one survey last week.
Acting Labour leader Michael Cullen said in a statement received on Monday that his party welcomed several aspects of Anderton's speech.

Cullen said he interpreted it as meaning the Alliance had abandoned any ambition to replace Labour as the major opposition party. "That means (Anderton) recognises Labour must be the focus in an alternative government to the national-led coalition."
"I would emphasise that Labour does not see the two parties forming a single entity for political purposes. We each have our proper role to play," he added.
"But Anderton's speech makes it more likely that Labour can look forward with confidence to leading a stable government..."
Labour leader Helen Clark was travelling in China and Hong Kong over the weekend. Monday is a public and market holiday in New Zealand.
